policy: Each concept retains its original audited definition plus two equivalent alternative retrieval clues. Clues do not change the accepted answer terms or award credit for a typo.

clues.text: A study concerns every adult in a town. What name is given to the entire group of interest?
An investigation aims to describe all 240 members of a club, not just those interviewed. Name the full group.
Every one of 180 households in a defined area is measured rather than only a subset. Name this investigation.
An investigation observes every unit in the defined group. Selection-based sampling variation is avoided, but measurement errors remain possible.
Of 400 pupils at a school, only 40 are chosen and surveyed. What is the name for these 40 pupils?
In a study of 800 trees, the 25 selected and measured trees form what kind of group?
These are the individual rainfall observations as first recorded, before totals or averages are calculated.
Name the unprocessed measurements, rather than grouped frequencies or a calculated mean.
The selectable entity in a survey design, such as one household when households are selected.
If classrooms, not individual pupils, are selected from a school register, each classroom plays this role.
An identification list of eligible people or items from which the researcher makes a selection.
A faulty employee register omits eligible workers; name the selection list that needs correcting.
This family of methods uses chance-based selection rather than a researcher's judgement.
A selection mechanism relies on a fair lottery, rather than convenience; name the general chance-based approach.
From a complete numbered list, distinct positions are drawn so every possible group of the required size has the same chance.
This design makes every possible subset of n units equally likely, not merely each individual unit equally likely.
A random initial list position is followed by a fixed step through the ordered entries.
For 600 numbered units and 30 selections, choose a random start among 1–20, then take every twentieth unit.
Split the population into non-overlapping groups and randomly choose units separately within each group.
The researcher randomly selects 15 Year 12 pupils and 20 Year 13 pupils from separate verified registers.
One of the mutually exclusive population groups used before separate random draws, such as the whole of Year 12.
This is a single subgroup in a partition of a population, rather than an individual person selected from it.
Interviewers recruit available volunteers until each fixed group target is filled; there is no random draw within groups.
A survey stops after recruiting 40 willing adults and 20 willing younger visitors without chance-based selection.
Participants are included because they are present and willing at the time, with no fixed subgroup targets.
A pupil asks the next 20 available people outside the canteen and sets no age-group counts.
A design systematically favours some eligible members over others, potentially distorting survey estimates.
Workers absent from the register cannot be picked even if the lottery over the listed workers is fair. Name this selection problem.
Which type of sample closely resembles the target population in characteristics relevant to the research question?
A group selected for a survey mirrors the population in the particular characteristics needed for valid conclusions. What type of sample is it?
Two well-chosen chance-based subsets of the same pupils yield different mean heights even though neither draw is incorrect.
Name the natural differences between statistics from separate valid random selections, distinct from systematic bias.
When every twelfth record is selected after a random start, name the fixed gap of twelve positions.
For 500 ordered invoices and a desired 50, the constant selection step is ten. Name this step quantity.
A subgroup forming 30% of a population receives 30% of the planned overall survey size before random selection within the subgroup.
A designer assigns numbers from each subgroup according to its share of the entire population. Name this allocation rule.
Eye colour and preferred transport mode are examples of this category-based information, not numerical measurement.
Bus route 25 is a label, not a count or amount. What type of information is the route code?
Distances measured in kilometres and numbers of goals scored belong to this broad category of information.
Measurements of time and counts of pupils are examples of this numerical type of information.
The number of visitors arriving in an hour can take only separate count values. What kind of numerical variable is it?
The result of one standard die roll is restricted to 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or 6, not every value between them. Name this variable type.
A runner's completion time can theoretically take any value in a suitable interval. Name this variable type.
The true length of a leaf can vary across an interval, even though a ruler records a rounded measurement.
Counts of results are organised into intervals such as 0–10 and 10–20 rather than individual values.
This display lists class intervals alongside counts of observations in each interval, rather than every original measurement.
The precise cut-off values at the edges of a grouped interval, such as 149.5 and 159.5 for measurements rounded to whole centimetres.
In the interval 10 ≤ x < 20, the endpoint values 10 and 20 play this role.
For a grouped interval running from 12.5 to 17.5, the value of this quantity is 5.
Subtract the lower edge of a class from its upper edge to obtain this quantity.
The value halfway between two interval endpoints, such as 15 for a class running from 10 to 20.
To estimate the mean from grouped measurements, each class can be represented by the average of its two endpoints.
